extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers (study section members reviewing NIH grant applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers evaluating NIH grant applications under the 2025 simplified peer review framework (effective for applications on/after Jan 25, 2025), reorganizing five regulatory criteria into three Factors with a two-numeric / one-binary scoring structure and an Overall Impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring structure: two numeric factors and one binary
rubrics_metrics.description: Framework reorganizes the five regulatory criteria into three Factors and replaces independent 1–9 scoring of all five criteria with a streamlined two-numeric / one-binary structure (effective for applications submitted on or after January 25, 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two Factors are scored numerically (1–9): Factor 1 (Importance of the Research) and Factor 2 (Rigor and Feasibility). Factor 3 (Expertise and Resources) is evaluated as a binary: 'Sufficient' or 'Gaps Identified' (with required explanation when gaps are identified). Reviewers then assign a single Overall Impact score (1–9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 1 — Importance of the Research (numeric, 1–9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combined assessment of Significance and Innovation to judge the importance of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scores should reflect both how important the research is in context (significance) and the novelty or newness of concepts, approaches, or applications (innovation). Note: a project lacking novelty may still be rated highly on this Factor if significance is strong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate the importance of the proposed research in the context of current scientific challenges and the strength of the scientific premise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
- Importance of the proposed research in the context of current scientific challenges.
- Whether the project addresses a critical knowledge gap, solves a critical problem, or generates a meaningful advance.
- Rigor of the prior research that justifies the proposed work.
- Strength of the scientific premise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate the novelty and originality of the concepts, approaches, methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
- Use of novel concepts, approaches, methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions.
- Refinement, improvement, or new application of existing approaches in a novel way.
- Note: a project lacking novelty may still be of critical importance and rated highly on the basis of significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 2 — Rigor and Feasibility (numeric, 1–9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Encompasses the Approach criterion and is split into Rigor and Feasibility sub-components to evaluate methodological quality and achievability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess both the likelihood that the research will produce unbiased, reproducible, robust findings (rigor) and whether the proposed work is achievable with the time, expertise, and resources available (feasibility). Both subcomponents inform the numeric Factor 2 score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of experimental design, analysis plans, and measures to ensure unbiased, reproducible, and robust findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
- Likelihood that the proposed research will produce unbiased, reproducible, robust findings.
- Quality of experimental design, including appropriate controls.
- Justification of sample sizes (power calculations).
- Plans for analysis, interpretation, and reporting (including pre-registration where appropriate).
- Plans for considering relevant biological variables (sex as a biological variable, age, ancestry).
- For studies involving humans or animals: rigor of intervention, outcome measurement, generalisability, sample diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether the methodology, timelines, and plans are realistic and achievable given available resources and potential challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
- Soundness and achievability of the methodology with the time, expertise, and resources available.
- Existence of plans to address potential problems and emerging challenges.
- For human-subjects studies: realism of recruitment and retention plans for diverse populations.
- For clinical trials: feasibility of timelines, enrollment milestones, and trial logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3 — Expertise and Resources (binary: Sufficient or Gaps Identified)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combines assessment of the Investigator(s) and the Environment to judge whether expertise and resources are adequate to execute the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated as 'Sufficient' or 'Gaps Identified' (when gaps are identified, reviewers must provide an explanation). This Factor merges the former 'Investigator(s)' and 'Environment' criteria into a single binary determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the qualifications, background, and team organization of the PI(s) and key personnel relative to the proposed work and career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
- Demonstrated background, training, and expertise of PI(s) and key personnel relative to career stage.
- For multiple-PI applications: quality of leadership coordination plans, governance, and complementarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of institutional resources, facilities, and the intellectual environment supporting successful project execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
- Whether institutional resources, facilities, and intellectual environment are adequate to ensure successful project execution.
- Subject availability, instrumentation, collaborative support, ongoing studies in related areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact Score (1–9)
rubrics_metrics.description: A single score reflecting the likelihood the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the relevant research field(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assigned after scoring the three Factors. Scale: 1 = exceptional, 9 = poor. The Overall Impact is not a mathematical function of the Factor scores; reviewers integrate Factor scores with their judgement to assess likely overall influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for human subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Required consideration (not scored) of protections for human subjects where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must evaluate and comment on human subjects protections when relevant, including ethical safeguards, risk minimization, consent, and related protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of women, minorities, and individuals across the lifespan
rubrics_metrics.description: Required consideration (not scored) of inclusion plans for diverse populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should comment on whether inclusion plans address representation of women, minority groups, and individuals across the lifespan and whether plans are justified or adequate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Required consideration (not scored) for projects involving vertebrate animals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate appropriateness of animal use, welfare considerations, and justification of species and numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Required consideration (not scored) of biohazard risks and mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers comment on identification of biohazards and adequacy of plans to mitigate risks to personnel and the environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Required consideration (not scored) evaluating how well resubmitted applications respond to prior critiques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess the quality and completeness of the applicant's response to previous review comments and whether the resubmission addresses prior concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Required consideration (not scored) for renewal (competing continuation) applications, assessing progress to date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate accomplishments relative to prior aims, productivity, and whether the project has advanced sufficiently to merit continued funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision adequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Required consideration (not scored) for revisions, assessing whether changes are adequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers judge whether the revisions adequately address the issues raised in the prior review and whether the revised aims/methods are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of key biological and chemical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Required consideration (not scored) that key resources are authenticated to ensure reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers comment on plans or evidence for authentication of cell lines, antibodies, reagents, and other critical biological/chemical resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget adequacy and justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Required consideration (not scored) of whether requested budget and justification are appropriate for the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should note if budget requests are unreasonable, insufficient, or otherwise raise concerns about feasibility or resource allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict-of-Interest Norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Norms requiring declaration and recusal for conflicts and strict confidentiality obligations for reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
- Reviewers must declare and recuse for personal, professional, financial, or institutional conflicts.
- Confidentiality of submitted applications and review discussions is a binding obligation; sharing applications with non-reviewers is misconduct.
